subject.title: [Refactor] Consolidate synthetic log formats across MCP service pipelines

question: Should the core OpenClaw tools MCP entrypoint and the Codex plugin compatibility adapter intentionally expose one stable diagnostic format, and which boundary should own it?
rationale: Current main already shares protocol-safe transport logging; making their remaining entrypoint diagnostics identical would create a cross-owner compatibility contract without evidence that users or tooling require one.

options.title: Keep ownership separate
options.body: Retain entrypoint-specific diagnostics unless a concrete consumer, output comparison, or user-visible mismatch demonstrates that a shared contract is needed.

options.title: Define a neutral contract
options.body: Introduce a narrowly scoped MCP entrypoint diagnostic formatter with focused tests proving both owners require the same stable output.

recommendation.title: Keep ownership separate
recommendation.body: Retain entrypoint-specific diagnostics unless a concrete consumer, output comparison, or user-visible mismatch demonstrates that a shared contract is needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The available public history most directly connects this account to the affected MCP surface and its ownership decisions.
